clue.text: Puts out smoke? One's lacking in p's and q's

definitions.text: One's lacking in p's and q's

indicators.note: letters put out of place no longer stand in their original order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
roke is an old and dialect word for smoke or vapour

explanation.surface: Someone who blows smoke about and has no manners, minding neither p's nor q's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'p's and q's' suggests etiquette, but it means the letters themselves: p and q have only descenders, so no upward pen stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstroke is the upward line made in handwriting; lower-case p and q are formed with tails going down instead.

clue.text: Tourer maybe, with haste filling notebook

indicators.note: something filling another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a tourer is a type of car, hence 'maybe'
to hie is to hasten

explanation.surface: A touring car rushing about with a notebook stuffed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cahier is the French word for an exercise book, borrowed into English for a notebook or report.

clue.text: Scots livid about mass censure

indicators.note: one thing about another goes round it, enclosing it

parts.note: blae is Scots for blackish blue or livid
M is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Scots, livid with anger, censuring the masses.
explanation.definitionFit: To blame is to censure or find fault with, and as nouns the two are also synonyms.

clue.text: Cross about euro, even ones spent? This one's worthless

indicators.note: one thing about another wraps round it

parts.note: a zo is a cross between a yak and a cow

indicators.note: spending the even-numbered letters uses them up, leaving only the odd ones behind

parts.note: the first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: Crossly complaining that a euro, once spent, is worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective for angry; it is the animal hybrid zo (also dzo), a yak-cow cross familiar from Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero is nothing, the number with no value at all, so it is the one that is worthless.

clue.text: Cheeky tyke of old, beatnik pursuing women

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so this piece comes second

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
a hipster was a hip person, a beatnik of the 1950s

explanation.surface: An impudent youngster of old, a beatnik chasing after women.
explanation.definitionFit: Whipster is an archaic term for a nimble, impertinent young fellow, a whippersnapper.

clue.text: Operant managed with three bugs? Only one

definitions.note: names one member of a group of bugs

indicators.note: managed here means handled and rearranged, as if put into new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone running a business with three bugs, though in the end there is only one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three bugs' seems to count insects; 'Only one' makes the definition a single member of the bug group.
explanation.definitionFit: Heteroptera is the insect suborder of true bugs, so a heteropteran is any single one of those bugs.

clue.text: Royal French and English tense, with loosely tinted edging woven on shield

indicators.note: an edging runs round the outside, so these letters border the others
loosely arranged letters are not held in their original order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher
FR is the abbreviation for French
E is the abbreviation for English
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A heraldic description: royal French and English emblems on a shield, with a woven tinted border.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry interfretted means interlaced, describing charges such as rings linked through one another on the shield.

clue.text: Cleric prayed fervently with no end of sincerity

indicators.note: something done fervently is wild and agitated, scrambling the order
with no means lacking, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter, removed from the other word

explanation.surface: A clergyman praying earnestly but without real sincerity.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the informal name for a chaplain, especially a military one, and so for any cleric.

clue.text: Cheeses keep tipping over on board?

indicators.note: on board a ship means inside a steamship, abbreviated with two letters around the cargo

parts.note: SS is a steamship, the ship one is on board
to tilt on is to keep on tipping over

explanation.surface: Cheeses that keep sliding over on a cheeseboard, or a ship's table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' does double duty: it signals the enclosing and provides SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a famous blue English cheese, so Stiltons are several such cheeses.

clue.text: King in suit that was turned up in card game once

indicators.note: turned up in a down entry means read from bottom to top
in places one thing within the other

parts.note: a coat is part of a suit, or a suit of clothes in a broad sense
R, rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king appearing in a suit that was turned over in an old card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' and 'suit' both sound like playing cards, but they give R and COAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Taroc, or tarok, is an old card game played with a tarot pack, now largely historical.

clue.text: G is this in rising triad here

definitions.text: G is this in rising triad here

indicators.note: rising in a down entry means read from the bottom upward
in places one thing inside the other

parts.note: a trine is a group of three, a triad
taken as written

explanation.surface: A music lesson: the note G is enclosed in this rising triad.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: in the answer as entered, the G is indeed surrounded by the reversed triad.
explanation.definitionFit: Engirt means surrounded or encircled, which is exactly the G's situation within the letters here.

clue.text: Bracteoles, colourless, bordering drainage channel

indicators.note: bordering means lying around the edges, so these letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: pale means lacking colour
ea is a dialect word for a river or Fenland drainage channel

explanation.surface: Pale little bracts growing along the edge of a ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: Paleae are the small chaff-like scales in grass flowers, botanically a kind of bracteole or small bract.

clue.text: Swimming, what a holiday-maker seeks in part of Australia

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: NT is the Northern Territory
a sun-seeking tourist wants a tan

explanation.surface: Swimming and sunbathing, as a tourist on an Australian beach does.
explanation.definitionFit: Natant is a formal or heraldic adjective for swimming or floating, from Latin natare.

clue.text: Cowpat maybe has disfigured green (gee not involved)

indicators.note: something disfigured has its shape spoiled and rearranged
letters not involved are left out of the word they sat in

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the letters to remove: one G and two Es

explanation.surface: A cowpat has spoiled the village green, though the horse (gee-gee) had no part in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip G, E and E out of green to leave R and N, then rearrange those with has.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharn is a dialect word for cow dung, of which a cowpat is one example.

clue.text: Lament what's dreadful about Government

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: dire means dreadful
G is the abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: Complaining about how dreadful the Government is.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song or lament, originally sung at funerals.

clue.text: Unit in clock, one directing course

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a timer is a clock-like device
unit and one both mean the number 1

explanation.surface: A component inside a clock, the part that directs its course.
explanation.definitionFit: A timoneer is a helmsman, the person at the tiller who steers a ship's course.

clue.text: Bit of meat from duck wrapped in the same (rolled)

indicators.note: something rolled over is turned round end to end
wrapped in means enclosed by the following piece

parts.note: the same as a duck: a score of nothing
a duck in cricket is a score of zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A cut of meat from a duck, rolled and wrapped like a roast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the same' refers back to duck: both mean nothing, so the second is NIL. A duck is a batter's score of zero in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Loin is a cut of meat from the back of an animal, between ribs and hindquarters.

clue.text: Smoke selection of free cheroots

indicators.note: a selection is a run picked out of the whole, here letters lifted from the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Have a smoke from a selection of complimentary cigars.
explanation.definitionFit: Reech is an old Scots spelling of reek, meaning smoke.

clue.text: Rotter takes in ceramist almost comprehensively defeated at cards

indicators.note: to take in is to hold inside, enclosing the next piece

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a rotter

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a potter works in ceramics

explanation.surface: A scoundrel tricks a potter and thrashes him at cards.
explanation.definitionFit: In piquet a player is capotted when they take no tricks at all, a total defeat called capot.

clue.text: Begin to contact a spiritual being, as Rev. Spooner might have it (8, two words)

indicators.text: as Rev. Spooner might have it
indicators.note: Dr Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of neighbouring words

parts.note: to wire someone is to contact them by telegram; its opening sound is traded
a fay is a fairy; its opening sound is traded

explanation.surface: Starting a séance, trying to get in touch with a spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the W and F of WIRE A FAY to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire away is an idiom inviting someone to begin speaking or asking questions.

clue.text: Hearing aid dispersing endless otic fog and rancor! (12, three words)

indicators.note: dispersing scatters things, breaking up their order
endless means without its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, losing its last letter
taken as written
taken as written, in its American spelling

explanation.surface: A hearing aid that clears the fog in the ear and the irritation that goes with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing aid' suggests a device, but it is a body part that aids hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of Corti, in the cochlea of the inner ear, holds the hair cells that turn sound into nerve signals.

clue.text: Agile SA native, nuts maybe about kisses, a cracker

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the next piece goes inside

parts.note: KP is a British brand of salted nuts, hence 'maybe'
to lip is to kiss
a ringer, or dead ringer, is slang for something excellent, a cracker

explanation.surface: A lively South African, nuts about kissing, a real cracker.
explanation.walkthrough: KP is a British snack brand known for its peanuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The klipspringer is a small, sure-footed antelope of southern Africa's rocky hills, its name Afrikaans for rock jumper.

clue.text: Allowing unrestricted view lover naughtily limits window blind

indicators.note: limits means sets the bounds of, enclosing what lies within
behaving naughtily means misbehaving, out of proper order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating meaning suitable for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: A louvre is a window or shutter of slanted slats, letting air in while blocking the view.

clue.text: Sea-serpent? Head in ocean almost seen rearing

indicators.note: rearing up in a down entry means reading from the bottom upward
in places one piece inside the other
almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the sea is the ocean
the poll is the head

explanation.surface: A sea monster rearing its head up out of the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that this is a loose, archaic sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellops is an old name for a serpent or fish of uncertain identity, used by Milton among his monstrous serpents.

clue.text: Votary teaching religion in service, rising

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
rising in a down entry means read from the bottom upward

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force, an armed service
RI is religious instruction, a school subject

explanation.surface: A devotee who teaches religion in the armed forces and gets promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, religious instruction, is the old British school subject now usually called RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A votary is someone bound by vows, and a friar is a member of a religious order who has taken them.

clue.text: Sleuth's passion, I admire new clothes?

indicators.note: clothes cover what is inside, so the letters are wrapped within the words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A detective's love interest, admiring someone's new clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Irene Adler, of 'A Scandal in Bohemia', was to Sherlock Holmes always 'the woman'.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene Adler is the one woman Holmes admired, the nearest the famous sleuth had to a passion.

clue.text: Most of fine — man weaves — in filaments perhaps

definitions.text: Most of fine — man weaves — in filaments perhaps

indicators.note: weaving interlaces strands, mixing them into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written: the whole mixed together
taken as written, losing its last letter; removed from the whole
taken as written; also removed from the whole

clue.text: Guardian out abroad, in Turkey

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

clue.text: Damage that's terminal in watch you repair last

clue.text: Stomachs a transparent plastic turned after end of dinner

clue.text: Timeless cage for flounders?

clue.text: Avoid old clergyman spouting Latin initially

clue.text: Minos's mum recalled regret having love with dad

clue.text: Padre, forgetting middle bit, droned terribly, getting slower and softer
